question: Is there a permitted, reproducible public-data path connecting AI/digital infrastructure with renewable energy in Indonesia or Southeast Asia?
answer: Partially: the announcement/financing layer and the physical-generation context layer are each reproducibly accessible; the layers between them — operating facility registries for data centers, renewable-procurement claims, and certificate/REC registries — have no permitted, reproducible public path that we could verify this session. gem_supply_context.what_this_is: A subtotal of GEM-API-LISTED operating generation units (unit-level MW sums) in Peninsular Malaysia after state-name normalization. It is INCOMPLETE: the API asset list has no solar/wind/hydro class, units below GEM thresholds are unlisted, and units with no API state are shown separately as unassigned.
what_this_is_not: NOT a generation mix (the API omits solar/wind/hydro entirely).
NOT evidence of electricity supplied to any specific data centre (no supply linkage exists in any dataset inspected).
NOT a complete inventory of Malaysian generating capacity.
gem_supply_context.coverage_gap: The GEM Ownership API asset list contains no solar, wind or hydro assets at all; bioenergy is the only renewable class present. This is an API coverage gap, NOT evidence that Southeast Asia lacks renewables.
gem_supply_context.geography_notes: State spellings normalized (Melaka/Malacca, three Negeri Sembilan variants, Penang/Pulau Pinang). Labuan is East Malaysia and excluded. Units whose API state is missing are reported in unassigned_mw, not silently dropped.

exploratory_example.name: GDS Nusajaya Tech Park Data Center Project, Phase 1 (Johor, Malaysia)

layer_1_financing.title: Bank of China (Malaysia) contributes to $272.12 million syndicated green loan for Phase 1 of GDS Nusajaya Tech Park Data Center Project
layer_1_financing.green_label_note: AidData narrative quotes the facility agreement as a 'syndicated green term loan' (Dec 2023). This is GREEN-LABELLED FINANCING — a loan-market label quoted from the record. It is NOT evidence of renewable procurement, RECs, or the facility's energy mix; no procurement data was found in any inspected source.
layer_1_financing.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0), stated in the 'License' sheet of AidDatas_CLG_LMIC_Dataset_v1.0.xlsx (verified 2026-10-30)

what_this_is_not: NOT a generation mix (the API omits solar/wind/hydro entirely).
NOT evidence of electricity supplied to any specific data centre (no supply linkage exists in any dataset inspected).
NOT a complete inventory of Malaysian generating capacity.
layer_2_grid_context.note: Context only, NOT a supply link and NOT a generation mix: this is a subtotal of GEM-API-listed operating units (incomplete by construction); no dataset inspected connects this facility to any specific generator.

non_claims: No claim that GDS Nusajaya procures renewable energy (no procurement data found).
No claim that the facility is physically supplied by any specific plant.
The 'green loan' label is quoted as a financing attribute, not as an energy attribute.
The absence of solar/wind in the GEM API is a coverage gap, not evidence about Malaysian renewables.
exploratory_example.claim_status: two documented context layers (financing record + grid asset snapshot) with NO causal or contractual connection asserted
